key_insight: The paper proposes a modular fault-tolerant quantum computer built from Cornucopia code blocks that keeps ultra-high encoding rates while supporting universal logical operations at low overhead.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path to scalable quantum hardware by combining high-density quantum memory with reusable, individually addressable logical-gate gadgets.
method: Use the [[2844,1426,18]] Cornucopia code as a module that stores 1,426 logical qubits per block.
Connect blocks with bridges and exploit translation symmetry to build reusable gadgets that address 1,422 logical qubits individually.
Provide three logical instruction sets: basic, high-throughput, and fixed-extractor.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, excluding magic-state factories, a module able to execute any basic instruction averages 4.1 physical qubits per logical qubit, versus 3.0 for memory alone.
watch_item: The low-overhead benefit may depend on the cost and integration of magic-state factories, which are excluded from the reported qubit accounting.
paper_title: A modular quantum computer based on Cornucopia codes
